Oracle Database 19c 인스턴스의 메모리(SGA와 PGA)와: A 10-step animated lesson that dissects the memory (SGA and PGA) and processes (server processes and mandatory background processes) of an Oracle Database 19c instance. It also covers memory management methods (AMM, ASMM), PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT, Linux HugePages, and a case where the instance will not start after the SGA was enlarged.
The SGA was raised from 8G to 12G and the instance will not start after the restart. Dissect the instance's memory and processes in 10 steps.

SGA를 12G로 늘리고 재시작했더니 인스턴스가 뜨지 않는다: The SGA was raised to 12G, and after the restart the instance will not start
정기점검 날, 버퍼 캐시가 모자란다는 분석에 따라 dbserver02의: On maintenance day, following an analysis that the buffer cache was too small, sga_target on dbserver02 was raised from 8G to 12G and the database restarted. But startup ends in an error and the instance does not come up. The server has 32G of physical memory, which is plenty.
\"메모리가 넉넉한데 왜?\"에 답하려면 인스턴스의 메모리가 어떻게 생겼: To answer "why, with so much memory?", you need to know what the instance's memory looks like and how Linux hands that memory out. This lesson opens up the memory and processes that make up an instance, one by one.
\"인스턴스와 데이터베이스\" 4장면에서 NOMOUNT는 SGA를 잡고: In scene 4 of "Instance and database", NOMOUNT was the step that allocates the SGA and starts the background processes. This failure is stuck at that very first step.
SGA는 모두가 함께, PGA는 프로세스마다 따로: The SGA is shared by all; each process has its own PGA
Concepts에 따르면 <span class=\"term\">SGA</: According to Concepts, the SGA (System Global Area) is memory shared by all server and background processes. Things many sessions must share, such as cached blocks, parsed SQL and the redo buffer, live here.
<span class=\"term\">PGA</span>(Program: The PGA (Program Global Area), in contrast, is memory used by a single process. As the documentation says, there is one PGA for each server process and background process. Session-only workspace, such as for sorting, is allocated here.
리눅스로 보면 SGA는 공유 메모리, PGA는 각 프로세스의 개인 메모리: Seen from Linux, the SGA is shared memory and the PGA is each process's private memory. The shared memory in scene 7, "Memory", of the Linux anatomy is the SGA.
SGA 안: 버퍼 캐시, 공유 풀, 리두 로그 버퍼, 그리고 나머지 풀: Inside the SGA: buffer cache, shared pool, redo log buffer, and the other pools
Concepts가 꼽는 SGA 구성 요소는 <span class=\"te: The SGA components listed in Concepts are the buffer cache (data blocks), the In-Memory area (optional), the redo log buffer, the shared pool, the large pool, the Java pool and the fixed SGA (internal housekeeping). The Administrator's Guide also names the Streams pool as an SGA component.
공유 풀에는 파싱된 SQL과 PL/SQL이 있는 라이브러리 캐시, 데이터: The shared pool holds the library cache with parsed SQL and PL/SQL, the data dictionary cache, and more. The lesson "Parsing and the shared pool" looks at it in detail. On the STARTUP screen, Database Buffers is the buffer cache size and Redo Buffers the redo log buffer size.
구성 요소별 크기는 <code>V$SGAINFO</code>로 볼 수 있: Sizes per component are in V$SGAINFO. The Administrator's Guide says to query V$SGAINFO and V$SGA_TARGET_ADVICE when sizing the SGA.
+ 버퍼 캐시 · 공유 풀 · 리두 로그 버퍼: + buffer cache · shared pool · redo log buffer
+ 라지 풀 · Java 풀 · Streams 풀 · 고정 SGA: + large pool · Java pool · Streams pool · fixed SGA
PGA 안: 커서의 실행 상태와 정렬·해시 작업 공간: Inside the PGA: cursor execution state and sort and hash work areas
Concepts는 PGA를 몇 영역으로 나눕니다. <span class=: Concepts divides the PGA into areas. The private SQL area holds bind variable values and query execution state, and SQL work areas are used for sorting (sort area), hash joins (hash area) and bitmap merges. With a dedicated server connection, session information (the UGA) is also in the PGA.
큰 <code>ORDER BY</code>나 해시 조인은 작업 영역을 크: A large ORDER BY or hash join uses a big work area. If the work area is too small, the rest is processed by writing to the temporary tablespace, which is slower. That is why total PGA grows with the number of sessions times what they do.
SGA는 정해 둔 크기로 시작할 때 잡히지만, PGA는 세션이 일하는 만: The SGA is allocated at its set size at startup, but PGA grows and shrinks with the work sessions do. That is why the two are considered separately when planning memory.
+ 개인 SQL 영역 (바인드 값, 실행 상태): + private SQL area (bind values, execution state)
앱이 리스너를 거쳐 접속하면 그 접속만을 위한 <span class=\": When an app connects through the listener, a server process is created just for that connection. Concepts explains that with a dedicated server, each client connection is served by one and only one server process. Twenty clients means twenty server processes.
서버 프로세스는 SQL을 파싱하고 실행하며, 필요한 데이터 블록을 데이터: The server process parses and executes SQL, and reads the data blocks it needs from the data files into the buffer cache. The documentation says server processes read data blocks from data files into the database buffer cache. Results go back to the app through that process's PGA.
리눅스 <code>ps</code>에서 <code>oracleORCL (: In Linux ps, oracleORCL (LOCAL=NO) is a server process that came in through the listener. In DBA labs stage 3, lesson 27, you trace a session's SPID to this process.
필수 백그라운드 프로세스: 각자 맡은 일이 하나씩: Mandatory background processes: each has its own job
Concepts가 꼽는 필수 백그라운드 프로세스는 다음과 같습니다. <b: The mandatory background processes listed in Concepts are: the PMON group (PMON and the cleanup processes CLMN and CLnn), LREG (registers the instance with the listener), SMON (system-level cleanup, instance recovery), DBWn (writes dirty buffers), LGWR (writes the redo log buffer to the online redo log), CKPT (records checkpoint information), MMON and MMNL (AWR-related work), RECO (resolves distributed transaction failures), and PMAN.
문서는 이 밖에 MMAN, DIAG, VKTM, DBRM, PSP0 같은: The documentation adds that other mandatory processes such as MMAN, DIAG, VKTM, DBRM and PSP0 are covered in the Database Reference. Since the instance cannot survive losing one of them, whether ora_pmon_ORCL is running is the first check of whether the database is alive.
리눅스 실습 1단계 레슨 6에서 <code>ps -ef | grep pm: You do this check with ps -ef | grep pmon in Linux labs stage 1, lesson 6. Because LREG registers with the listener, a service showing up late in the listener status right after startup is also this process at work.
~ 하나라도 죽으면 인스턴스 중단: ~ losing any one stops the instance
메모리 크기를 누가 정하나: AMM, ASMM, 수동: Who sizes memory: AMM, ASMM, manual
Concepts와 Administrator's Guide는 세 방식을 설: Concepts and the Administrator's Guide describe three methods. Automatic memory management (AMM) sizes SGA and PGA together with a single MEMORY_TARGET; automatic shared memory management (ASMM) sets SGA_TARGET and a PGA target separately; manual sets each pool size directly. The documentation recommends AMM when SGA plus PGA is 4 GB or less.
PGA에는 두 값이 있습니다. <code>PGA_AGGREGATE_TAR: The PGA has two settings. PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET is only a target and can be exceeded; PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT is a hard limit. According to the documentation, when it is exceeded Oracle terminates calls from the sessions with the highest untunable PGA allocations.
dbserver02처럼 SGA가 8G인 서버는 ASMM(SGA_TARGE: A server like dbserver02 with an 8G SGA uses ASMM (SGA_TARGET), because the HugePages in the next scene cannot be used together with AMM.
HugePages: SGA를 큰 페이지에, 스왑 없이: HugePages: the SGA in large pages, never swapped
리눅스는 메모리를 보통 4KB 페이지로 나눠 줍니다. 8G SGA를 4K: Linux normally hands out memory in 4 KB pages. Splitting an 8G SGA into 4 KB pages makes a very large number of page table entries. According to the Linux Administrator's Reference, with HugePages the pages are locked in memory and never swapped out, TLB hits increase, and the kernel does less bookkeeping with fewer page table entries.
HugePages는 미리 개수를 정해 잡아 둡니다. 필요한 수는 SGA: HugePages are reserved in advance as a fixed count. The number needed is the SGA size divided by the large page size (grep Hugepagesize /proc/meminfo, usually 2 MB), rounded up. dbserver02 reserved 8G ÷ 2 MB = 4096 pages with vm.nr_hugepages. The documentation says AMM and HugePages are not compatible, and recommends disabling Transparent HugePages.
Oracle MAA 모범 사례는 <code>USE_LARGE_PAGES=: The Oracle MAA best practice is USE_LARGE_PAGES=ONLY. With it the whole SGA must come from HugePages, and if there are not enough the instance does not start at all. The point is to notice right away rather than come up half on normal pages.
사례: SGA는 12G인데 HugePages는 8G 분량: Case: the SGA is 12G, but HugePages cover only 8G
1장면의 원인입니다. SGA를 12G로 늘렸지만 <code>vm.nr_h: This is the cause from scene 1. The SGA was raised to 12G, but vm.nr_hugepages stayed at 4096, enough for 8G. With USE_LARGE_PAGES=ONLY, as the Linux Administrator's Reference says, the database fails to start when HugePages are insufficient. The documentation notes that an alert log message then provides the necessary information on HugePages.
해결은 계산부터입니다. 12G ÷ 2MB = 12,288MB ÷ 2MB: The fix starts with arithmetic: 12G ÷ 2 MB = 12,288 MB ÷ 2 MB = 6144 pages. As root, change vm.nr_hugepages to 6144 in the sysctl configuration file and apply it, confirm HugePages_Total is 6144, then start the database. If memory is fragmented and not all pages can be reserved at once, a reboot may be needed.
SGA 크기를 바꾸는 변경 요청에는 \"HugePages도 같이\"를 꼭: Any change request that resizes the SGA must also say "and HugePages". Linux labs stage 2, lesson 14 walks through computing and setting the 4096 pages. The documentation points to hugepages_settings.sh (MOS 401749.1) for the calculation.
SGA는 모든 프로세스가 공유하는 메모리로 버퍼 캐시, 공유 풀, 리두: The SGA is memory shared by all processes, holding the buffer cache, shared pool, redo log buffer and more; the PGA is private memory, one per process, holding execution state and sort and hash work areas. Each connection gets a server process, and the mandatory background processes split the writing, recovery, registration and statistics work.
리눅스에서 SGA는 HugePages에 올립니다. AMM과는 함께 쓸 수: On Linux, the SGA goes into HugePages. They cannot be combined with AMM, so ASMM is used, and whenever the SGA size changes the HugePages count is recalculated too.
이 레슨의 상자 하나하나가 다른 레슨의 주인공입니다. 버퍼 캐시와 LGW: Each box in this lesson stars in another lesson: the buffer cache and LGWR in "The journey of a COMMIT", DBWn and CKPT in "Checkpoints", and the shared pool in "Parsing and the shared pool".
